End-to-End (E2E) Use Cases ​

This document strictly defines the E2E use cases that are covered by our Playwright test suite (frontend/e2e/).

Document-First Approach: Any new feature that requires E2E coverage MUST be documented here as a use case before the Playwright test is written or updated. This ensures our tests accurately reflect intended user behavior.

Core Workflows ​

1. Dashboard Navigation (dashboard.spec.ts) ​

Objective: Verify that a user can successfully log in, access the dashboard, and create a basic project.

  • Pre-conditions: User is unauthenticated.
  • Steps:
    1. User navigates to the application root (/).
    2. User clicks "Sign in with Google" and completes the Firebase Auth Emulator flow (or uses custom token in staging).
    3. User verifies they are redirected to the main dashboard displaying "Your Projects".
    4. User enters a project name in the "Create Workspace" input and submits.
    5. User clicks the newly created project card in the grid.
  • Expected Outcome: User is successfully redirected to the "Project Dashboard" view for the specific project.

2. Project Modals & Script Parsing (project-modals.spec.ts) ​

Objective: Verify that users can edit project metadata and ingest a raw script using the "Paste Script" modal, bypassing the standard blank script flow.

  • Pre-conditions: User is logged in.
  • Steps:
    1. User creates a new project and navigates to the Project Dashboard.
    2. User clicks the "Settings" button to open the Project Settings Modal.
    3. User updates the project name and description, and clicks "Save Settings".
    4. User verifies the updated name appears in the header.
    5. User clicks "Paste Text" to open the Paste Script Modal.
    6. User inputs a title (e.g., "Episode 1: The Beginning") and raw script text (e.g., "INT. COFFEE SHOP...").
    7. User clicks "Create Script" and waits for the "Analyzing..." status to complete.
  • Expected Outcome: The parser successfully processes the text, the modal closes, and the user is redirected into the Unified Studio with the correct script title displayed in the header.
  • Environment Note: AI responses are mocked in local/dev but hit real endpoints in staging.

3. Full Orchestrator Workflow (studio-orchestrator.spec.ts) ​

Objective: Verify the entire end-to-end automation workflow from a blank script all the way to a rendered video, ensuring human-in-the-loop approvals function correctly.

  • Pre-conditions: User is logged in and inside the Unified Studio for a newly generated script.
  • Steps:
    1. User clicks the "Automate Workflow" button and selects "Guided Mode".
    2. User approves step_scenes. System mocks/runs director generation.
    3. User approves step_audio. System mocks/runs ElevenLabs voiceover generation.
    4. User approves step_visuals. System mocks/runs Imagen generation for scenes.
    5. User approves step_video. System mocks/runs FFmpeg stitching.
    6. User verifies the "Final Render" video player appears in Cinema Mode.
  • Expected Outcome: The stepper successfully advances through all stages, properly gating execution behind user approval clicks.

4. YouTube Publishing & Editor (studio-publishing.spec.ts) ​

Objective: Verify that a user can edit YouTube metadata and publish a finalized video directly to YouTube.

  • Pre-conditions: User is logged in with a linked YouTube account.
  • Environment Note: Real external API tests run ONLY in the staging environment.
  • Steps:
    1. User waits for the Orchestrator to reach step_publish.
    2. User clicks "Open Metadata Editor".
    3. User edits the title, description, and tags, then clicks "Approve Metadata".
    4. System queues the publish action.
  • Expected Outcome: The video payload is transmitted to the backend orchestrator successfully, and the UI displays a success toast.

Manual Studio Operations (studio-manual.spec.ts) ​

These tests verify the granular, manual controls within the Unified Studio, bypassing the automated orchestrator.

5. Cast & Location Management ​

Objective: Verify that users can manually configure the vibeMap for characters and locations.

  • Pre-conditions: User is logged in with an active script.
  • Steps:
    1. User opens the "Cast & Locations" modal from the Studio Header.
    2. User edits the physical description prompt for a character.
    3. User clicks "Generate Character Image" (AI image generation is mocked).
    4. User verifies the character thumbnail updates in the modal and timeline.
    5. User assigns a specific ElevenLabs voice ID to the character.
    6. User clicks "Preview Voice" and verifies audio playback is triggered.

6. Scene & Visual Generation ​

Objective: Verify that users can manually create scenes and generate individual visual assets.

  • Pre-conditions: User has a raw script with no scenes.
  • Steps:
    1. User clicks "Run Director" to manually break the script into scenes.
    2. User selects a scene in the timeline.
    3. User clicks "Generate Image" in the Visual Stage (Imagen generation is mocked).
    4. User verifies the scene card updates with the new image.
    5. User toggles the Visual Stage to "Video Mode".
    6. User clicks "Generate Video" for the same scene (Gemini/Kling generation is mocked).
    7. User verifies the scene card updates with a video player.

7. Manual Audio & Video Rendering ​

Objective: Verify the manual export and stitching flow.

  • Pre-conditions: User has scenes, visuals, and voice configurations ready.
  • Steps:
    1. User clicks "Generate Audio" in the Studio Toolbar to render the full timeline voiceover.
    2. User clicks "Export Video" in the Studio Toolbar.
    3. User waits for the export progress bar to complete (FFmpeg stitching is mocked).
    4. User switches view mode to "Cinema".
    5. User verifies the "Final Render" video player appears and plays back the stitched video.

Failure & Edge Case Workflows ​

5. Critical API & Billing Limits (failure-states.spec.ts) ​

Objective: Ensure the platform degrades gracefully and informs the user when critical external dependencies fail or quota is exceeded.

  • Pre-conditions: User is logged in with a mock account configured to simulate failures.
  • Steps:
    1. Billing Limit: User attempts to run an Automation, but their mock account has 0 credits. Verify the UI displays an "Insufficient Credits" modal.
    2. YouTube API Timeout: User attempts to publish, but the mocked YouTube API returns a 504 Timeout. Verify the UI displays a contextual error message allowing retry, rather than hanging indefinitely.
  • Expected Outcome: Clear error boundaries prevent silent failures.

6. Client-Side Error Logging (error-logging.spec.ts) ​

Objective: Ensure that unhandled exceptions and captured client-side errors are correctly formatted and sent to the Cloud Logging integration.

  • Pre-conditions: User is interacting with the application in an environment configured with a mocked Cloud Logging endpoint.
  • Steps:
    1. User performs an action that triggers a simulated error (e.g., clicking a hidden "Force Error" debug button or simulating a failed fetch response).
    2. Verify that the UI displays a generic fallback error boundary or toast notification to the user.
    3. Verify that an HTTP request (or Firebase function call) is dispatched to the Cloud Logging integration containing the correct structured payload (error message, stack trace, user ID).
  • Expected Outcome: Errors are gracefully caught and transmitted to the logging service without exposing sensitive stack traces to the end-user.
